problem_addressed: Malaysian-born persons of Indian origin without citizenship documents are excluded from school enrolment, formal employment, healthcare subsidy and the eKasih welfare register
structural_cause: Historic under-registration of estate births, loss of records on estate closure, and a case-by-case adjudication model with no caseload management
target_group: Undocumented and stateless persons of Indian origin born in Malaysia
eligibility: Malaysian-born; priority order: children of school age, students, persons with disabilities, elderly applicants, widows and single-parent households (Doc B Tab 4A)
delivery_mechanism: One-stop JPN-JPM service desks in every state and federal territory, mobile registration teams to former estate settlements and urban-poor localities, and active case management to resolution
supporting_agencies: Prime Minister's Department (delivery secretariat); Ministry of Education; Department of Social Welfare; state governments; legal-aid NGOs
output: Verified caseload baseline published within 9 months; 15 one-stop desks operational; mobile teams deployed; monthly published case statistics
outcome: Reduction in the number of Malaysian-born persons of Indian origin without resolved documentation status and in median case cycle time
duplication_assessment: Does not duplicate: JPN already adjudicates, but no case-management layer or published caseload exists. Runs on existing JPN adjudication authority
missing_design_information: Verified opening caseload; current median cycle time; the legal-aid capacity required per case
preliminary_feasibility: High for the desks and case management. LOW for any clearance-rate guarantee - citizenship is a Ministerial discretion

problem_addressed: Children from low-income Indian households enter Year One materially less prepared, and the gap compounds
structural_cause: Cost, transport and information barriers to preschool enrolment; no Indian-specific enrolment audit exists
target_group: Children aged 4-5 in low-income Indian households
eligibility: Household income in the bottom 40% by DOSM definition; needs-based, applied on income not ethnicity, with outreach targeted to communities with low enrolment
delivery_mechanism: Enrolment fee subsidy, transport support and meal support delivered through existing registered preschool platforms (KEMAS, PERPADUAN, MOE preschools and registered private providers), with SJKT and community organisations as the referral channel
supporting_agencies: KEMAS (Ministry of Rural and Regional Development); Department of National Unity; state education departments; community organisations
output: Baseline enrolment audit in Year 1; subsidised places rising to approximately 12,800 children per year by Phase 3; annual school-readiness screening
outcome: Higher preschool participation and improved school-readiness at Year One entry among low-income Indian children
duplication_assessment: Runs on existing national preschool platforms; adds a targeted subsidy and outreach layer. Overlaps with existing preschool fee assistance - the subsidy must be net of any assistance already received
missing_design_information: Actual current enrolment rate for this cohort; provider capacity by district; unit fee variation by provider type
preliminary_feasibility: High. Delivery capacity exists; the constraint is enrolment outreach and subsidy administration

programme_name: SJKT Safety and Learning Environment Programme
problem_addressed: Physical condition and digital capability vary widely across the 528 SJKT, and no complete audited condition record exists
structural_cause: Historic under-capitalisation of national-type schools and a maintenance model that responds to applications rather than to audited condition
eligibility: All SJKT; remediation prioritised strictly by audited safety risk
delivery_mechanism: Condition audit of every SJKT, a published prioritised remediation schedule, safety-critical works, digital learning facilities and a trained coordinator per school
supporting_agencies: Public Works Department; state education departments; school boards and PIBG; MITRA (equipment)
output: 528 condition audits completed and published in Phase 1; prioritised remediation schedule published; safety-critical works completed; digital facility and trained coordinator in every SJKT
outcome: Every SJKT meets a defined safety and learning-environment standard
stated_cost_in_source: RM50m maintenance (existing); no incremental cost stated
duplication_assessment: Substantially overlaps the existing national dilapidated-schools programme and the RM50m SJKT maintenance line. MIB 2.0 funds only the audit, the digital layer and the incremental safety gap not covered by existing programmes
missing_design_information: The SJKT share of the national dilapidated-schools programme (VAL-11); the actual condition distribution across the 528 schools
preliminary_feasibility: High. This is conventional public works with an established delivery agency; the risk is scheduling, not capability

programme_name: Multi-Faith Community Institution Safety and Compliance Programme
problem_addressed: Faith-based and community institutions serving Malaysian Indian communities face unaddressed safety, accessibility and regulatory-compliance problems; temples affected by estate displacement also face distinct tenure, relocation and registration issues
structural_cause: Facilities are often built and maintained by community subscription without access to public safety-capital programmes; legal and administrative pathways differ by institution and faith, while some temples occupy land with unresolved tenure
target_group: Faith-based and community institutions serving Malaysian Indian communities in high-need localities, including Hindu temples, mosques and surau serving Indian Muslim communities, churches, Sikh gurdwaras, Baha'i facilities and other eligible institutions
eligibility: Documented education, welfare, youth, elderly, cultural or other public-interest community service; demonstrated safety, accessibility or compliance need; participation is voluntary and requires state, institutional and any applicable religious-authority consent; eligibility is needs-based with no fixed allocation by religion
delivery_mechanism: Common track: joint safety, accessibility and compliance audit plus matched funding for safety-critical works. Differentiated track: documentation and referral of temple and estate-legacy tenure, relocation and registration cases to competent state authorities. Institution-specific coordination follows the relevant legal and religious-administration regime. Funding excludes worship, proselytisation, ceremonies, devotional fixtures and doctrinal activity
supporting_agencies: Department of National Unity and National Integration; state governments and local authorities; Public Works Department; Fire and Rescue Department; relevant Islamic religious authorities; Hindu, Christian, Sikh, Baha'i and other representative or trustee bodies
output: Multi-faith facility map and consent framework completed; participating institutions audited; prioritised safety works list and recipient grants published by institution type; safety-critical works completed with matched funding; temple and estate-legacy documentation compiled for state referral
outcome: Participating institutions meet defined safety and accessibility standards and can lawfully continue eligible community-service functions; distinct temple and estate-legacy cases enter a documented state-referral pathway
duplication_assessment: No single federal programme covers this multi-faith scope. Jurisdictionally sensitive: land, local government and religious institutions operate under differentiated state legal and administrative regimes
missing_design_information: Verified number and type of eligible institutions; state and religious-authority consent requirements; faith-type distribution; split between common safety works and temple or estate-legacy referral; revised cost envelope
preliminary_feasibility: MODERATE-LOW. Delivery depends on state and institution-specific consent. The current 1,200-facility and RM44.400m assumptions pre-date a verified multi-faith map and must be recalibrated. Federal support must be confined to life safety, accessibility, compliance and documented public-interest community-service spaces—not religious practice

problem_addressed: Students complete SPM without a structured understanding of available pathways and qualified candidates lose places through incomplete or late applications
structural_cause: Career guidance capacity is thin in the schools serving this population, and admissions systems assume informed applicants
target_group: Indian students in the two years before completing secondary education
eligibility: All Indian students in participating schools; intensive support prioritised by household income
delivery_mechanism: Structured career profiling in Form 4-5, application clinics for matriculation, university, polytechnic, community college and TVET admissions, and follow-through to placement confirmation
supporting_agencies: Ministry of Higher Education; state education departments; TVET institutions; professional associations
output: Career profiling delivered to participating cohorts; application clinics held in each state; placement outcomes published by pathway
outcome: Higher proportion of Indian SPM leavers entering a confirmed post-school pathway within twelve months
duplication_assessment: Complements existing MOE career guidance; adds capacity and follow-through rather than a parallel service
missing_design_information: Current post-SPM destination data for this cohort - which does not exist and is itself a first deliverable

problem_addressed: Young people leave school into low-wage work with no structured route into skilled employment; training is not connected to employment outcomes
structural_cause: Training is funded by seat rather than by outcome, with no retention or employment tracking and no stipend, so low-income trainees cannot afford to complete
target_group: Indian SPM leavers not proceeding to tertiary education
eligibility: SPM completion; household income in the bottom 40%; commitment to the full programme including tracking
delivery_mechanism: Training seats in existing accredited TVET and STEM institutions, a completion stipend, employer-linked apprenticeships, and mandatory tracking from intake through certification to twelve months of employment
supporting_agencies: Ministry of Higher Education; TVET institutions; Ministry of Education; employers and GLCs; HRD Corp
output: Approximately 5,000 enrolees in Phase 1, 10,000 in Phase 2 and 15,000 in Phase 3 (30,000 cumulative); apprenticeship placements; a published tracking series
outcome: Higher certified completion and employment at or above the indexed wage threshold twelve months after certification
duplication_assessment: Runs on existing accredited TVET capacity and the Cabinet-agreed easy-path decision. Adds stipend, apprenticeship brokerage and tracking. Must not duplicate HRD Corp-funded employer training
missing_design_information: Current Indian TVET enrolment and completion rates; employer apprenticeship appetite by sector
preliminary_feasibility: MODERATE-HIGH. Seat capacity exists; the constraint is employer apprenticeship supply and tracking discipline

problem_addressed: Access to matriculation and other pre-university pathways is contested and the underlying intake data are not published in disaggregated form, so neither the community nor government can verify the position
structural_cause: Absence of published disaggregated intake data makes the actual constraint unidentifiable, and competing unverified figures circulate
target_group: Qualified Indian applicants to matriculation and other pre-university pathways
eligibility: Qualified applicants; navigation support prioritised by household income
delivery_mechanism: Publication of an annual disaggregated intake and offer series; applicant navigation support; a review of pathway adequacy reported to the Task Force
supporting_agencies: Ministry of Higher Education; matriculation colleges; Public Service Department (scholarships)
output: Annual published intake and offer series by pathway; navigation support delivered; adequacy review tabled
outcome: Qualified applicants are not lost to the system for informational or procedural reasons; the actual constraint becomes visible and addressable
stated_cost_in_source: 1,116-seat sub-quota; at least 2,000 offers per intake
duplication_assessment: No duplication. The 90:10 framework is unchanged and no additional seats are requested - this programme requests transparency and navigation, not reallocation
missing_design_information: Verified Indian matriculation offer and intake series (VAL-05); the true attrition point between qualification and enrolment
preliminary_feasibility: High for transparency and navigation. The seat-count question is deliberately left to evidence, not asserted

problem_addressed: Graduates without professional networks convert qualifications into professional employment at lower rates
structural_cause: Network dependence in professional entry, especially in law, finance, medicine and technology
eligibility: Graduates within three years of completion; prioritised by household income
delivery_mechanism: Structured mentoring by established professionals, professional-association placement partnerships, and preparation for professional entry examinations
supporting_agencies: Professional associations; universities; employers; Ministry of Human Resources
output: Mentoring pairings established; placement partnerships signed; participants tracked to professional employment
outcome: Higher conversion from qualification to professional employment
duplication_assessment: Complements existing graduate employability programmes; the Indian-specific element is the mentor network
preliminary_feasibility: MODERATE. Depends on volunteer professional supply

problem_addressed: Households receive assistance from multiple agencies at different life stages without any coordination, so support relieves a problem without changing the household trajectory
structural_cause: Programme-centred rather than household-centred administration; no single household record; no follow-through
target_group: Low-income Indian households facing two or more simultaneous barriers
eligibility: Household income in the bottom 40%; two or more concurrent barriers across documentation, education, employment, housing or debt; voluntary consent-based enrolment
delivery_mechanism: A designated Progression Navigator per enrolled household at a caseload of 150 households, a single consent-based household progression record, coordinated referral to existing programmes, and periodic progress review
supporting_agencies: Department of Social Welfare; Ministry of Human Resources; Ministry of Housing and Local Government; MITRA; state welfare departments
output: Approximately 120 navigators and concurrent capacity for 18,000 households in Phase 1, rising to approximately 400 navigators and concurrent capacity for 60,000 households by Phase 3; cumulative reach depends on case duration and turnover; case-management system operational
outcome: Enrolled households demonstrate measurable movement in income stability, employment, savings or housing security
duplication_assessment: Does not deliver benefits itself - it coordinates access to existing programmes. Overlaps conceptually with existing social-welfare case management, which must be mapped before deployment
missing_design_information: Actual multi-barrier household counts; navigator recruitment and training pipeline; consent-and-privacy design
preliminary_feasibility: MODERATE. Case management at this scale is demanding. Coverage is deliberately capped at approximately 10% of the estimated low-income household population, not universal

programme_name: Microenterprise Growth and Vendor Capability Programme
problem_addressed: Businesses receive financing but remain microenterprises, unable to meet the compliance, certification and scale requirements of larger markets and government supply chains
structural_cause: Financing addresses capital but not capability: compliance, certification, bid preparation and consortium formation are unaddressed
target_group: Indian-owned microenterprises and small businesses with growth potential
eligibility: Registered business; demonstrated trading history; growth intent; selection on capability assessment, not ethnicity alone
delivery_mechanism: Structured business advisory covering financial management, compliance, digitalisation, quality certification and procurement readiness; consortium formation support; bid preparation assistance. Financing continues to run on existing TEKUN, SPUMI, AIM and BRIEF-i rails
proposed_owner: Ministry of Entrepreneur and Cooperatives Development
supporting_agencies: TEKUN Nasional; AIM; Bank Rakyat; SME Corp; MAICCI and KLSICCI; Ministry of Finance (procurement policy)
output: Approximately 5,000 enterprises through structured advisory over six years; certified vendors registered; consortia formed; participation in federal procurement measured and published
outcome: Growth in enterprise revenue, employment and successful bids among participants
stated_cost_in_source: 500 certified vendors; 2% procurement share; RM100m contracts
duplication_assessment: No duplication of financing - MIB 2.0 adds no new lending facility. Overlaps with SME Corp vendor development, which must be used as the delivery vehicle rather than replicated
missing_design_information: Baseline enterprise survival and growth rates; SME Corp capacity
preliminary_feasibility: MODERATE. NOTE: the ethnic procurement set-aside and 2% participation quota in the source draft are REJECTED on Article 8 grounds; participation is measured and published, not mandated

programme_name: Household Savings and Asset Accumulation Scheme
problem_addressed: Low-income households hold negligible financial buffers, so a single shock returns the household to crisis and no asset base accumulates
structural_cause: Income volatility and the absence of any matched-savings instrument reaching this population
target_group: Low-income Indian households with capacity to save
eligibility: Household income in the bottom 40%; enrolment in a qualifying savings product; matching capped per household per year
delivery_mechanism: Matched savings, structured on the MIB 2017 design of a seed fund providing matching booster units in a qualifying unit-trust or savings product, with matching ratio varying by income band and a minimum lock-in
supporting_agencies: Permodalan Nasional Berhad (subject to its own commercial decision); Bank Negara Malaysia; AIM; Department of Social Welfare
output: Approximately 15,000 participating households in Phase 1 rising to 50,000 by Phase 3; matched contributions credited; participation and balances reported annually
outcome: Increase in the proportion of participating households holding a defined minimum financial buffer
stated_cost_in_source: RM500m; RM5,000 per household to 100,000 households (REJECTED as a mischaracterisation)
duplication_assessment: No existing matched-savings instrument reaches this population. Must be designed so it does not duplicate or displace existing SARA/STR cash transfers, which serve a different purpose
missing_design_information: Product design; PNB's willingness to participate; the matching ratio schedule; MOF concurrence
preliminary_feasibility: MODERATE. The instrument is genuinely provisional: it requires MOF design approval and PNB's commercial agreement. It is NOT a revival of a lapsed scheme - it is a new instrument modelled on an MIB design that was never implemented

programme_name: Housing Access and Estate Legacy Resolution
problem_addressed: Families displaced from plantation estates occupy insecure tenure in urban peripheries, paying rent that builds no equity, with unresolved legacy land and compensation grievances
structural_cause: Estate closure without transition, tenure or asset settlement; allocation criteria in national housing programmes that do not recognise displacement history
target_group: Estate-displaced and low-income Indian households in housing insecurity
eligibility: Household income in the bottom 40%; documented estate-displacement history or current tenure insecurity; needs-based criteria applied without ethnic restriction
delivery_mechanism: An estate-displacement legacy review producing an actionable administrative record; facilitated access to existing affordable-housing and rent-to-own programmes; deposit and transaction assistance; targeted site infrastructure
proposed_owner: Ministry of Housing and Local Government
supporting_agencies: State housing agencies; SJKP; Ministry of Plantation and Commodities; state land offices; Department of Social Welfare
output: Legacy review completed and tabled; approximately 6,000 households assisted into affordable housing or rent-to-own over six years; revised allocation criteria adopted in participating states
outcome: Increase in secure tenure among assisted households
duplication_assessment: Housing units themselves are funded through existing national and state housing programmes. MIB 2.0 funds the legacy review, access facilitation, deposit assistance and targeted site works - not construction
missing_design_information: Number of households in scope; state housing agency capacity and willingness; land status of legacy sites
preliminary_feasibility: MODERATE-LOW. Depends heavily on state cooperation and on land matters within state jurisdiction. Deliberately the most conservatively scoped programme in the portfolio

problem_addressed: Indian representation in the federal civil service is 3.7% (2024) against a population share of approximately 6.5%
structural_cause: JPA states the binding constraint is very low application volume from non-Malay candidates, who nonetheless record the highest appointment success rates - i.e. the failure is at application, not selection
target_group: Qualified Indian graduates and school leavers eligible for public service entry
eligibility: Meets standard JPA entry requirements; support is open and merit-based with no adjustment to entry standards
delivery_mechanism: Career awareness campaigns through schools, universities and community networks; application guidance and completion support; examination and interview preparation; mentoring by serving officers; publication of an annual grade-disaggregated composition series
supporting_agencies: Public Service Commission (SPA); Ministry of Higher Education; Ministry of Education; universities; professional associations
output: Application volumes from Indian candidates published annually; preparation programmes delivered; annual grade-disaggregated composition series published
outcome: Indian share of the federal civil service rises from 3.7% (2024) toward a range of 4.2%-4.8% by Year 6
stated_cost_in_source: 4.5% by Year 2; 7% by Year 6 (REJECTED as undeliverable)
duplication_assessment: No existing targeted programme exists, which both source documents state and which is corroborated. Runs entirely within existing JPA recruitment processes
missing_design_information: Current application volumes by ethnicity; the attrition point in the application funnel
preliminary_feasibility: HIGH for the pipeline work, which is inexpensive. The TARGET, not the programme, was the defect: 7% by Year 6 would require approximately 43,000 net additional officers and is rejected

problem_addressed: Representation at entry does not translate into representation at senior grades
structural_cause: Career-long development and mobility opportunities are unevenly accessed
target_group: Serving Indian officers in the federal civil service
eligibility: Serving officers; merit-based selection into development programmes
delivery_mechanism: Access to existing executive education, specialist training, cross-ministry exposure and structured mentoring, with participation monitored and published by grade band
output: Participation in development programmes published by grade band; mentoring pairings established
outcome: More even grade distribution over time
duplication_assessment: Uses existing INTAN and JPA development programmes; adds monitoring and outreach only
missing_design_information: Current grade distribution by ethnicity - not published and a first deliverable
preliminary_feasibility: High. Very low cost; the deliverable is largely transparency

problem_addressed: No body owns cross-ministry outcomes for this agenda, publishes the numbers, or answers for them
structural_cause: Coordination units placed in line ministries lose convening power over other ministries; MITRA has programme funds but no authority over ministries that hold the levers
delivery_mechanism: A Prime Minister-chaired Task Force meeting quarterly, supported by a delivery secretariat in the Prime Minister's Department, with each programme retaining its accountable ministry and accounting officer
supporting_agencies: All lead ministries; MITRA; Ministry of Finance; Implementation Coordination Unit
output: Terms of reference approved; secretariat established; quarterly meetings held; dashboards published within 14 days of each meeting; annual report to Parliament
outcome: Programmes stay on schedule and off-track programmes are escalated and corrected within one quarter
duplication_assessment: Does not replace MITRA, which continues as an executing agency. The Task Force coordinates and holds to account; it does not assume MITRA's financial authority
missing_design_information: Terms of reference; secretariat establishment approval; the escalation protocol
preliminary_feasibility: HIGH for establishment. The residual risk is that quarterly PM chairmanship is not sustained, which is the single largest delivery risk in the portfolio

problem_addressed: Neither government nor the community can currently verify what has changed, because baselines and disaggregated outturn data do not exist
structural_cause: Programmes report activity, not outcomes; ethnic disaggregation is inconsistently published
delivery_mechanism: A baseline survey in Year 1, a public progress dashboard, a Data Protection Impact Assessment before any household record operates, an independent mid-term evaluation at end-Year 3, a final independent evaluation in Year 6, and annual Auditor-General audit
supporting_agencies: DOSM; Ministry of Economy; National Audit Department; independent evaluators
output: Baseline survey published; dashboard live; DPIA completed and published; mid-term and final evaluations published; annual audits tabled
outcome: Every KPI has a verified baseline and a published outturn series
duplication_assessment: No duplication. This is the measurement layer both source drafts call for and neither costs
missing_design_information: Survey design and DOSM collaboration; dashboard specification

programme_name: Revival of the RM500m / RM5,000-per-household interest-free loan scheme for 100,000 IB40 households
retain_decision: REJECTED. The instrument it claims to revive never existed in the form described (CNF-007). Replaced by PRG-11, which reconstructs the MIB's actual matched-savings design

programme_name: PNB successor equity fund toward population proportionality
retain_decision: REJECTED. Rests on the unsupported 1.5bn AS1M claim (CNF-008). Cabinet cannot direct a corporate entity's unit allocations, and no verified predecessor allocation exists to restore

programme_name: Procurement set-asides and a 2% vendor participation quota for Indian SMEs
retain_decision: REJECTED as designed. Serious Article 8 equality exposure for an ethnically-defined federal set-aside. Capability, certification and consortium elements are retained within PRG-10 with participation measured, not mandated

programme_name: Consolidated IB40 registry merging the documentation database with poverty targeting
retain_decision: REJECTED. Linking citizenship-status records to welfare eligibility creates discrimination and data-protection risk and would chill take-up among the target population (CNF-032). Replaced by two separate systems within PRG-01 and PRG-09

programme_name: Income-floor guarantee for IB40 households unable to work
retain_decision: REMOVED from MIB 2.0. A guaranteed minimum income floor for one ethnic group is a national social-protection policy question that exceeds this blueprint's scope and would require its own Cabinet consideration. Households unable to work are referred to existing national social assistance through PRG-09
